Procurement reference MCE-26-041  |  Revision 2.1
MERIDIAN CIVIC ESTATES  AND  HARBORLIGHT FIELD SERVICES

An editable working agreement for monitoring occupied public buildings, responding to equipment alerts and documenting maintenance outcomes. This issued copy incorporates the negotiated winter-access arrangements.

cells.text: Northgate Library; Canal House; Eastbank Depot
Signed change order; clauses; schedules; explanatory figures

body.text: Using this agreement

Clauses 1-8 set the delivery obligations. Schedules A-C define prices, response windows and evidence requirements. Appendix D contains the acceptance form and Appendix E records the approved change procedure.

Navigation: scope and access (page 2); operational responsibilities (page 3); Schedule A, charges (page 4); Schedule B, service windows (page 5); Schedule C, evidence (page 6); Appendix D, acceptance (page 7); Appendix E, changes and execution (page 8).
Controlled-copy notice
All organisations, contacts and operational records in this agreement are fictional. Blank signature fields are intentional. A blank field is not evidence of approval.
1  Scope, access and delivery

Covered assets. The supplier shall monitor the listed sensors, inspect alert histories and issue one monthly service record for each site. Physical replacement of plant is excluded unless separately authorised under clause 8.

Access readiness. The client shall provide a named escort and safe access during the agreed service window. An unsuccessful visit caused by denied access is rescheduled once without a second call-out charge; the original response clock is paused only for the documented access delay.

Priority assessment. Priority is determined by operational impact, not by the number of alerts. A fire-system interface alert is escalated immediately to the client duty officer; this agreement does not replace emergency services.
Completion evidence. A job is complete only when the service record identifies the asset, arrival time, action taken and verification reading. A photograph without an asset reference is insufficient.
Definitions

cells.text: A human response confirming ownership of the incident.
A qualified operative reaches the nominated site reception.
The asset is returned to service or a client-approved safe workaround is active.
Monday-Friday, excluding the public holidays stated in Schedule B.
One auditable record per job, including any linked follow-up visit.

body.text: An acknowledgement is not attendance. Meeting an acknowledgement target does not stop the attendance clock. Schedule B defines the separate targets.
Boundary example

If a critical alert arrives at 16:50 and the operative arrives at 18:10, attendance is 80 elapsed minutes. It is not measured from the next business day. A separate routine request received at the same time follows the routine window.
2  Operational responsibilities
Supplier obligations

Competence and cover. HFS shall maintain an on-call roster and provide replacement cover when an assigned operative becomes unavailable. Subcontracting does not transfer responsibility for evidence or response times.
Each operative carries a current site induction record. Remote advice may support an attendance but cannot replace an expressly required physical inspection.
Client obligations
Site information. MCE shall maintain the access register, nominate a duty officer and disclose planned closures. The supplier must confirm receipt of a closure notice.
Known closures are listed against a site, not inferred from another site's timetable. The library and depot do not share a public-entry policy.
Joint review

Monthly review. Both parties shall reconcile open jobs, disputed charges and repeat alerts by the fifth business day of the following month. A disputed charge is held outside the undisputed monthly amount.
The review pack includes a list of unresolved items with named owners. Silence after circulation does not constitute acceptance of an unresolved charge.
Change control

Authorised changes. Only the named commercial signatories may vary scope or price. An operative's service note is not a purchase order. Use the process in Appendix E before undertaking chargeable additional work.
Urgent safety action may proceed to make an asset safe, but permanent replacement still requires separate written approval. Record the boundary between the two.
Escalation contacts
Client duty desk: civic-duty@example.invalidSupplier dispatcher: dispatch@example.invalidCommercial review: procurement@example.invalid
Schedule A  Charges and payment
All amounts are in GBP and exclude tax unless explicitly stated. Quantities are contractual units, not forecasts. The credit is deducted before tax.
Charge rules
A routine call-out outside the base scope is GBP 145.00 per authorised attendance. The first 45 minutes are included; subsequent time is GBP 22.50 per completed 15-minute block.
Travel within the three named sites is included. Materials require an itemised approval and are charged at evidenced cost without a handling uplift.
Invoice example
Payment is due 30 calendar days after receipt of a valid invoice. A credit must remain a deduction; parentheses do not indicate an optional amount.
Schedule B  Service windows and response targets
Targets are measured separately. Critical incidents use elapsed time at all sites. Routine work follows the applicable site window. All times are local.

Example: a routine Canal House request received Friday at 18:30 has 30 service minutes accrued by 19:00. Its remaining acknowledgement allowance resumes in the next open window. This example does not change the critical targets.
Schedule C  Evidence and service review
Each record must connect the reported condition to the action and the verified outcome. A closed status without evidence is reopened for review.

                                                 up visit.
